name: History
description: American and world history, from ancient empires to the modern era.

lessons.title: The American Revolution
lessons.body:
Between 1765 and 1783, thirteen British colonies broke away to form the United States.

## Road to war
- **Stamp Act (1765)** and **Townshend Acts** taxed the colonies, sparking the cry “no taxation without representation.”
- **Boston Massacre (1770):** British soldiers killed five colonists, including Crispus Attucks.
- **Boston Tea Party (1773):** the Sons of Liberty dumped British tea into Boston Harbor.

## The war
- Fighting began at **Lexington and Concord** in April 1775.
- The **Declaration of Independence**, written mainly by **Thomas Jefferson**, was adopted on **July 4, 1776**.
- The victory at **Saratoga (1777)** convinced **France** to join the war on the American side.
- The British surrendered at **Yorktown (1781)**; the **Treaty of Paris (1783)** ended the war.
keyFacts: The war began at Lexington and Concord in 1775.
Thomas Jefferson was the main author of the Declaration of Independence.
Saratoga (1777) was the turning point that brought France into the war.
The Treaty of Paris (1783) ended the war.

lessons.title: Ancient Egypt
lessons.body:
Ancient Egyptian civilization grew along the **Nile River**, whose yearly floods left rich soil for farming.

## Key ideas
- Rulers were called **pharaohs** and were seen as gods on Earth.
- The **Great Pyramid of Giza** was built for the pharaoh **Khufu** around 2560 BCE. It is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing.
- Egyptians wrote in **hieroglyphics**. The **Rosetta Stone**, with the same text in hieroglyphic, Demotic and Greek, let **Jean-François Champollion** decode them in 1822.
- Bodies were preserved as **mummies** for the afterlife.

## Famous pharaohs
- **Hatshepsut**, a female pharaoh known for trade expeditions to the land of Punt.
- **Tutankhamun**, whose nearly intact tomb was found by **Howard Carter** in 1922.
- **Ramesses II**, a great builder who fought the Hittites at Kadesh.
keyFacts: Egypt depended on the yearly flooding of the Nile.
The Rosetta Stone helped Champollion decode hieroglyphics in 1822.
The Great Pyramid of Giza was built for Khufu.
Howard Carter found Tutankhamun’s tomb in 1922.
